utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, assisted by Case Manager Sebastiaan van Hooydonk, and we also with us again today the intern, Ms. Mia Slogar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Ms. Deirdre Montgomery, appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Miroslav Cuskic, appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. If there are no preliminary matters, could we go into closed session so the witness could be escorted back to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, there is just one very short matter. When we were reviewing the documents, we found out that P2320 MFI, the document -- the document was admitted as MFI'd due to our objection concerning the application of Rule 66(B). I would like to inform the Trial Chamber and the parties that we are now withdrawing this objection, and if the Trial Chamber wants me, I can provide the reasons for that, but I don't think it's necessary. I mean -- I'm in your hands, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the document can be de-MFIed. P2320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It was admitted through -- it was offered by Mr. Hannis during the cross-examination of Witness Macar. It was quite sometime ago. But, when we were reviewing the documents, I found that this document is MFI'd. I thought it was de-MFIed in the meantime but since it was not, we are withdrawing our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm content with your --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- being willing to withdraw it without because, of course, I can't remember what the document was and what the issues were so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So can we take it that Your Honour makes the order, that the MFI is lifted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please close the blinds.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, you will recall on Friday I spent some time taking you through the document which was the list of the SDB employees for being paid in June and those who had, by August, disappeared. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose you showed me that document, but I cannot recall it precisely now. You -- you did show me some lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, the only reason I'm going back to this is because Mr. Krgovic challenged me to where you'd said that these people remained. And at page 25413 of the transcript, which was on the Tuesday, so quite early on, you were asked by Mr. Krgovic at line 14: "Please tell me about the ethnic composition of the state security centre personnel in early 1992?" You said: "The ethnic composition mostly remained the same as far as we're concerned. Croatian, Muslim and Serbian personnel, et cetera." And then later down the page: "And after 1992, after April 1992, was this ethnic composition in the State Security Services centre the same as before?" And you said: "Yes, it basically remained unchanged." And then you were shown the document, which is 2D184. Do you accept, sir, having seen the other documents, that you made an error there?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the composition during that period did not change. And it didn't, as far as I know. Later you showed me some lists and gave me some information about a later period. But during that period, as far as I know, those people were around. I used to see them around, and I don't know who stood in for who or who changed their job. I know that some people found other jobs. But, in principle, the people remained, because I saw them around.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move to another topic. The parade of the police, including the special police, on the 13th of May that I asked you about, and you said you didn't attend it but you were aware that the minister came down. I'd like you to look very briefly, please, at a report of this parade, which is 65 ter 122, document number 9 in our list. Can I ask, first of all, whether you read this report in "Glas"?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. It describes the march-past of the forces of the police. Apart from marking the day of service, it also had the purpose of acquainting the citizens of the Autonomous Region of Krajina with the forces that the police currently have and which they intend to persist in maintaining the peace and the stable security situation in this area. Now, do you accept, sir, that whatever you may say was the real relationship of the special police with the CSB Banja Luka, they were dressed in police uniforms, and they were intended to signal to the public that these were members of the police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As this text indicates, this is about appearances, as far as I can tell. The political motivation was to show that the police has a certain force, but, as you know, 90 per cent of these men were soldiers. I forgot to say when you asked me about my role in all that, after this parade - I don't know how long after it - I went to that command and I had the chance to see what it's like. That command had another military officer whom I failed to mention but nobody asked me either. Because all your questions were of the type, "isn't it?" Was so-and-so deputy, or was so-and-so this or that, but nobody asked me whether there were any more military officers in the command of that detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, sir, one last time, please, to just answer the questions I ask, not to volunteer information and not to go off on topics that I have not asked you about. I will explain to you again, for the third time, that Mr. Krgovic has the chance to re-examine you. Now, we continue, please, with this article. Is it your contention that of that huge parade, of which we have seen videos on a number of occasions, 90 per cent of the participants were military?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't referring to all participants in the parade. I'm talking about the people in these vehicles and the ones that were presented as special unit members, the drivers and others. Maybe up to 90 per cent were, indeed, military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We've already dealt with this on Friday and I'm not going to -- all right. Just continuing on this report: "As a symbol of the linkage of the security services and the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, air force planes did a fly-past over Banja Luka at the time of the march-past." The army and the special police were separate but linked. That's the situation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already explained that wherever there was activity of military nature, there was the military and -- was in charge of these activities. There was subordination in place, according to which all forces, no matter who, were resubordinated to the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I accept that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: To the army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody had an -- was at an equal footing with the army. You are presenting it as if it were a tea party or something. No, it was about obeying orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I accept entirely that in combat action where the police and the army were actually fighting, then it was the army who had control. But in other circumstances, sir, and I suggest the special police are part of those circumstances, they were, in fact, separate though acting together in a common cause? Would you agree that? And you can simply say no, if you don't.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on then, please. And let's go back to the topic I was dealing with on Friday; namely, who was in charge of this unit. Could you have a look now, please, at 65 ter 10647. Document number 12. This is dated the 22nd of May, 1992. It's addressed to the chief. And we need to go to the second page in English. Somebody called Mr. Dusan Rokvic was proposing these people. And do we see there that it was approved by the chief of the centre, Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If Mr. Zupljanin was no more than a paymaster for this force, why would anybody bother to get his approval for who went into the platoon? Into the special police. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document basically has nothing to do with the special police. This was drafted for the following reason: People were to be employed as police officers. These people were refugees. I think that this man, Tutoric, was a police officer in Croatia. They were refugees from the Croatian part so it was normal for them to be received into service at the CSB. Milan Tutoric was platoon commander and they stayed together. Only salaries were taken care of directly. It was about their future status. They were supposed to be active-duty police officers. This has nothing to do with the others. This doesn't even account for 10 per cent of the personnel because we see the number of people. There are nine on the list. This is what I was talking about. They were admitted to the police as active-duty police officers because they had been police officers wherever they had fled from, Croatia or someplace. So this was basically a humane act of a social nature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, the actual question was nothing do with -- I'm going to show you exactly why these men are, in fact, members of the special police. But the question, sir, which you just didn't answer, is why, if this is a military unit under the control of Colonel Stevilovic and the military, Stojan Zupljanin's approval should be needed to put these men into the special police?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I kindly ask Ms. Korner to show where this document states what she is saying that it states.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a misinterpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, on the face of it, that is what the document suggests, and Ms. Korner is putting to him what the document seems to say. I -- I -- I'm not sure I follow your objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Sir, can you answer the question, please. Why should Stojan Zupljanin, who you say has no authority over the special police, be authorising people to go into the special police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously you don't have a good translation. This reads: "I propose that employees be admitted to permanent employment who are members of the special police detachment with the Banja Luka CSB." So they are already there. He is taking people from the military establishment upon the proposal of Dusan Rokvic. This is very different from a unit that was -- did not have this status. If everybody had permanent employment with the centre, then this document would not be necessary. This document shows that this was a formality and that people submitted applications to be transferred to the -- to permanent -- to a permanent post with CSB Banja Luka. This was taking over people from the detachment to the Banja Luka CSB, as active-duty members. The detachment had a total strength of 150 or 160 men. And this is only about nine. By the way, I listened to those tapes and I found a number of wrong -- wrong interpretations --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, don't go off -- do not go off on a tangent, please. Forget the tapes. I have a lot to get through with you today, so you forget the tapes until I go back to them myself. Now, do you accept, do you agree, therefore, that these nine men were, in fact, members of the special police and apparently remained in the special police until certainly after July?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that they were special police members. That is, members of the special unit. But also that they got permanent employment with the Banja Luka centre. The -- these are two different statuses, as different from the other members of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask that this document be marked and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, but before we do that, may I suggest that the witness be invited to read the word at the -- at the head of the signature block in which Mr. Zupljanin's signature appears and see how it is interpreted. Because I'm bearing in mind Mr. Krgovic's objection and the witness's answer or explanation up to this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The word beginning with S at the head of the signature block --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you read, please, just so we can get a translation, after the -- the word that begins with S there.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this word means.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just read it, please. Just read it.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In block letters it says "Stojan Zupljanin" and there's somebody's initials above it. Whose initials these are, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Read, please, not the name Stojan Zupljanin but the word that you can see in capital letters.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "saglasan nacelnik centra."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Which interpreted means approved, or in agreement, chief of centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. The document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2409, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Have a look next, please, at -- well, yes. We'll just confirm this. Document 65 ter 20333, at tab 54. Oh, sorry, 20323. List of members of the special police detachment, the Banja Luka Security Services Centre. Go, please, to the third page in English, and I believe it's the same page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have the original or the hard copy? Because I find it a bit tiring to sit like this leaning forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm very sorry, but we don't have hard copy -- unless Mr. Krgovic can give you his copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I have the hard copy of the Prosecution evidence. Therefore, we can give it to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Unmarked. Not if it's marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I haven't got time to check it. I'm just going to take Mr. Krgovic's word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 54. Turn to the third page, you'll see the 5th Platoon.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All the men on that list were in the 5th Platoon, were they not, of the special police? And were still there because we can see this must have been, although it's not a dated document, if you go to the penultimate page, you will see that there's a list of people who had been deleted after the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, can we go to page 4 in English. Yes. Somebody's done it. Your Honours, I'm going to be coming back to this list on a number of occasions so I wonder if it could be marked and admitted at this stage. I just wanted to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: There doesn't seem to be any objection. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2410, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next, please, can we look at document which is at 65 ter 2733, tab 15A.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dated 25th June, addressed to Stojan Zupljanin, and it's a request from Mr. Novakovic of the Petrovac Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff to Mr. Zupljanin, do you agree, asking for him to send a special purposes police detachment to Krupa?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number is it in your bundle?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 15A. Have a look at the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find this particular one under 15A.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, just look --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have found it. It's 15. I can't believe it. There's no 15A here. The last one that I can see is 7A, then 12A.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'll do my best to read from the screen provided it's enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we enlarge the left-hand side, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you accept that this is a request to Mr. Zupljanin from Mr. Novakovic in Petrovac to send a special purposes police detachment?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads here that the Ministry of the Interior is sending this to Mr. Stojan Zupljanin personally. But I don't see that this document was actually received nor that anyone had been assigned to undertake these tasks. Normally once an assignation is made, then the name of the person who is going to implement this is specified.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. That is not the purpose of -- of this document, nor the question, as you well understand, sir. This document reflects, does it not, the reality that Stojan Zupljanin organised, set up, and was in charge of the special police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It only says here that a request was sent to him. As for everything else that you have put into it, it's how you read it. This document states that only a request was sent to Mr. Zupljanin and that he didn't assign this to any particular person. So I don't see any of his instructions concerning this document. And this actually is up to the person who is the author of this document. I don't know if the title is correct. I don't know whether there was the Ministry of the Interior of the Krajina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask that this document be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection. First of all, Bosanski Petrovac municipality is not covered by the indictment. Therefore, it goes beyond the indictment framework. Secondly, this document was disclosed to us only after this witness came here to testify, and we didn't have an opportunity to see this document before. It falls into the category of what we call typically new evidence that is not on the 65 ter list, and we couldn't find it anywhere in the reports, whether it was, indeed, disclosed to us, and, if it was, when that was. Talking about the Prosecution 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, apart from the objections voiced by Mr. Krgovic, in terms of relevance, inasmuch as this is addressed to Mr. Zupljanin rather than emanating from him, why should it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all, we're checking on whether it was disclosed. Second, not until this witness turned up last week did anybody ever suggest to any witness that the whole of the special police was not a special police force at all, but a military force run and controlled by Colonel Stevilovic. It was disclosed - interrupting myself - on the 12th of February, 2009. Obviously because it was Zupljanin. We can't help it if their records are not that accurate. And, thirdly, this is one of a series of documents which, in our submission, shows that what the witness is saying is putting at its lowest unreliable. It goes entirely to the credit of the assertions he has made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we would remind you that we indicated last week that if you at any point prefer to stand, you are free to do so. I'm reminding you that if you prefer to stand at any point during your testimony -- sorry. I'm -- just in the event that you missed a part of what I said, you may stand at any point during your testimony if you find that more comfortable. Returning to the application to tender this document, the document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now can we look, please, at P1091, document 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is part of the saga --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 2733 is admitted as Exhibit P2411. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is part of the saga, sir, that you touched upon when you looked at the list of complaints against members of the special police. And this is a document in which Stojan Zupljanin tries to order the -- the SJB to release two members of the special detachment. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was sent shortly before I had contact with Mr. Tutus.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That may be so, sir. But do you agree, on the face of it, this is Stojan Zupljanin trying to order the SJB to release two members of the special detachment who have committed, apparently, crimes?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call it crimes. This was criminal activity and the suspicion was that it involved unauthorised appropriation of vehicles and that was the reason for bringing those people into custody. Due to that situation and the poor information that the special unit had, certain reactions were provoked and requests were made for those people to be released because it was believed that that was the standard skirmishes that people had with the police when they went in and out of pubs. And they believed that this was the way to reach an agreement with those people, provided there is no danger of their flight, to release them, on condition that they come back for additional interviews --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please answer the question put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was whether this was a request for those people to be released. One can see from it here that it was. And that they were obliged to report on their own, in order for the proceedings to go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If these were members of the military, as you suggest, why wasn't it Colonel Stevilovic or somebody from the 1st Krajina Corps command asking for the release?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is only logical for the centre chief to ask something from the SJB chief. However, Stevilovic couldn't order the chief of the SJB to do something. He had Stojan Zupljanin above him. This is a normal standard letter. And when I went to see Mr. Tutus, I thought that there was good reason for them to remain in custody. I don't see any problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, take it from me that we've seen in this case evidence of the military writing to the police or the courts asking for the release. The only reason that Stojan Zupljanin was the man asking or ordering the release was because these were police officers under his command and control. That's the situation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's have a look, please, now at the document you will find at number 10 in your bundle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 20th of May but it's -- it's the minutes of the meeting held on the 6th of May of 1992. And a copy, apparently, goes to your chief, Mr. Kesic, apart from anybody else. Did you -- did he discuss this meeting with you at all?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't talk about this meeting. You are giving me a document that I haven't read before, and I need some time to look what it is -- and see what it is all about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, well, I just want to --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Banja Luka, Gradiska, Grahovo ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you just go to the very end, please. Item number -- agenda number -- item number 3 on the agenda. The chief of the CSB, Stojan Zupljanin informed the members of the centre council that he had established a special counter-sabotage and counter-terrorist police unit about -- of about 150 to be deployed in those regions in the most complex security operations. The unit is made up of both active and reserve police and persons who fought on the Western Slavonia battle-fronts. So is it your contention that Stojan Zupljanin is lying to the assembled police who he has called for this meeting when he says he has set up a special unit?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I presume that this was more him boasting about this. He couldn't have set up a detachment because it had to be done based on a decision from higher authorities. He probably had a pivotal role in it but the setting up of the detachment itself had to be based on a decision taken by an assembly or the local government or whatever. As far as I know, the centre chief never had these kind of powers to set up such formations personally. He probably put it figuratively, "I set up," in order to boost his rating among other chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, he certainly couldn't set up, could he, a unit of special police without authority from the minister.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the rules and regulations, somebody has to take a decision at a certain level. I suppose whether it was minister or the government. But I think that it was primarily the government or the assembly. And when this decision was taken, I think it was taken by the government or the assembly. That's what the law says. I don't think that any individual, unless they have a proper decision from higher authority, can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Leaving aside that we've all seen that the ARK Assembly made a decision to set it up, Stojan Zupljanin himself personally could not have hired people or paid them without being authorised by the minister of the interior, could he?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this situation and how these issues were resolved in Krajina. You are asking me a leading question. Maybe you can ask me if I knew how it was resolved.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, you can easily find in the law who is authorised to issue this kind of decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am asking you, as a senior police officer of some 30 years' experience in the police, whether the minister would have to authorise the payment and recruitment of personnel for a special police unit. And if you don't know, then say so.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there should be or must be some additional decision only I don't know issued by whom. That's my assumption that it had to be based on a decision, on an order that came from a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And what about the words "the unit is made up of both active and reserve policemen and persons who fought on the Western Slavonia battle-fronts"?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The bulk of this unit was made up, was it not, of active or reserve police, not, as you say, military personnel?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite the opposite. The majority of the men were military.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this can be checked from personnel files.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Let's now go, please, jump forward because I'm still dealing with the same topic, this was Stojan Zupljanin's unit, in the sense that he was in command and control.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look now at the ending of it, at 1D00176 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that a question, what Ms. Korner has just said? Or is Ms. Korner testifying?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, my suggestion throughout - that's why I'm going through this rather tedious exercise - is that this is Mr. Stojan Zupljanin's unit. And that is the topic I'm dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Look, please, at 1D00176, document 27A. This is the order of the 27th of July from Mico Stanisic, who repeats in paragraph 2 that in accordance with his earlier order of the 23rd of July, "I hereby order immediately to remove," underlined, "from the minister of interior individuals who have been held criminally responsible for crimes." I'm emphasising that for a reason we'll see in a moment. Then item -- paragraph 4: "Immediately disband and place under the command of the army of the Serbian Republic all special units formed during the war in areas of Security Services Centres." Now, if, as you say, let's just concentrate on Banja Luka CSB, the unit there, whatever it was called, was actually under the control of the army, what was the purpose of Mico Stanisic ordering the disbandment of the unit who should then be handed over to the army?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously he was acting in accordance with an order issued on the 28th of July, or the 23rd of July. He is citing someone's order. And he is issuing an order to have this order carried out. And he says that the CSB is to participate in carrying out this order. I wish to add that in mid-July that unit has already been disbanded. The people were receiving pay but they had military billeting and military food. They had no more --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, don't offer that. I'm going to deal with when they were disbanded. Just, please, as His Honour Judge Delvoie asked you, answer the question that you are asked. If the CSB special police were, in fact, members of the military and not police at all, then what was the purpose of Mico Stanisic issuing this order?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, the government or the Assembly of Republika Srpska took a decision to disband all units that were not a part of the army. This meant all of them. They were seen as some kind of paramilitary formations. In order to carry this out in the field, all organs of authority in the field had to take part. Military police and so on. It's logical that the police receive an order from the government through the minister. It is also logical that military orders go down the military line of command.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You see I think you've -- I don't think you meant to, but you have, in fact, made the point. The government took the decision to disband all units that were not part of the army. And the CSB special police in Banja Luka were not part of the army, were they?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a part of the army. But its situation was specific. It was not a part of the establishment. Formally it was with the centre but actually was carrying out military orders. We were different from paramilitary organisations in other areas. It was actually under the command of military persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Look next, please, at P631, which is at 32. This is a report on the inspection of the CSB, and done by two inspectors who you met, as we'll see. Or one of them at least. If we look at the last page, Mr. Gajic and Mr. Mirosavic. 5th of August. I don't know whether you were present at the meeting of the -- or the period they were there between the 2nd and the 4th of August, were you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall whether I was present. Obviously this is a report written by someone. I do not see who the authors are here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I don't think it matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Go back, please, to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you see there the discussion about - I think it's in the first paragraph - the minister's order that we've just looked at. And Stojan Zupljanin wanting to know what the word "remove" means. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is it precisely?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Second page in your language, first paragraph. If you look at it on the screen, you'll be able to see it straight away.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 2? The first paragraph is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Begins "medjutim."

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, the first one. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, we'll get on a lot quicker, and you'll be here a lot less longer if you actually look at the documents on the screen where they can be highlighted for you. Now, do you see there he is querying, what "remove" means?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says is it's the only measure that we could have taken, and that was to remove them from the unit, from the war schedule, or either we could process them through military courts or the civilian organs. Now this is something else that I have here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I don't --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A report and another report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll tell you what, sir, you read to yourself just -- you just -- I don't know what you're looking at. If you look at the screen, then we will all be on the same page. Kindly have a look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we highlight, please -- no, not the first paragraph anymore. Can we highlight the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want you to read that, sir, either on the screen, or in -- in the -- in the bundle that you've got. The paragraph that begins: "Since the beginning of the war ..." Just read that to yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have finished reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Stojan Zupljanin and his officers, whoever were with him, are objecting, aren't they, to any idea that the CSB police, special police, should be disbanded?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that such discussions did take place and that many people from the command, from the unit, were against disbanding these units. I remember this. It was at some meeting or other. I know for a fact that it was agreed that the unit should be disbanded, and I was in favour of it. Practically, it was an undefined unit. It was neither here nor there. It was under the control of the military, but we were financing it. And there were certain problems with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just stop, please. Do you agree - that's all my question was - that Stojan Zupljanin and, as it's put, "his associates" were objecting to disbanding the special police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was, they were probably -- probably objected to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. From what you have read of this inspectors' report, were Stojan Zupljanin and his associates objecting to the disbanding of the special police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that what they said was, in fact, all positive. It had some positive activities and that a number of criminal procedures against these workers were suspended who had not been disciplined. It says that most of those who took part in the discussion believed that the Republika Srpska Assembly was -- request was unfounded. Regardless of this, the unit was disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Never mind that. I'll try one last time, and I have a reason for asking you this. Do you agree that Stojan Zupljanin and his associates, according to this report, did not want the unit disbanded?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to this line of questioning. The witness is asked to interpret this document and it's a meeting that he did not attend. If the Prosecutor wants him to answer, he should be asked to interpret this document and she should not suggest what -- something that is not in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As I understand the question, Mr. Krgovic, it is -- on the one hand, there is this document and its import; and, on the other is the thrust of the witness's testimony. And the question invites him to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll come -- can I help? I'll come directly to what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thanks, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that's the simplest thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You see, you told the Court at page 25459 of the transcript, which was last Wednesday, the question was -- it says there was some -- just listen, please, to the question. It says: "There was some resistance to the idea of disbanding the unit. Can you tell me who was for and who was against?" "A. I think I was in favour of disbanding it. I think there was disagreement within the centre itself. I believe that Mr. Stojan was in favour of disbanding it too." Now, how did you get that impression from Mr. Zupljanin given what he is clearly saying here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, I was showing a different document, from another meeting, not this document. The witness was asked to interpret another document, another meeting. That's my point. It was a meeting at which he was present and that's what he was interpreting. He was not asked to interpret something where he was not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I still think you are missing the point of the question, Mr. Krgovic. Please proceed, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, sir, it is wholly untrue, isn't it, that Stojan Zupljanin wanted the unit disbanded? He wanted the unit kept on.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was at a meeting where he was in favour of disbanding the unit but Djuro Bulic opposed this. His deputy or his assistant, I'm not quite sure what he was by function.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll come on to that meeting in a moment. So it's your assertion, anyhow, that he was in favour of disbanding it. Why did it matter whether he was in favour of disbanding it or not, if he had no control over them at all?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply, it was a discussion. Everyone had their opinion to state. The inspectors had their positions to present, and he, respecting the decision of the Republika Srpska government, he acted like an officer and some others believed this was not correctly done. And had he not obeyed the order, this would not have been implemented at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason why, if what you're telling the Court is the truth, this was a military unit under military command, Stojan Zupljanin didn't say to the inspectors or to anybody else, I don't know why you're talking to me about it. It's not my decision. This is a military unit.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because the unit was on the payroll of the centre. He was the one who had to resolve this issue. Here I saw somewhere that it had to do with payroll. Whether their status would be workers who are paid or -- normally he would be the one who would have to decide how the question was resolved financially. I know this was resolved, I personally made the payments, and they received payments until the 31st of the month.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Forget -- forget, please, about that. What I'm asking you is to -- can you think of any good reason why, at the very least, he didn't just say, I have nothing to do with these police. As you well know, I'm merely the paymaster. Any reason why he wouldn't have said that, if that was the case?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any reason for him to say that. Everyone knew that we were the ones who made the payments, and the army gave everything else. There is nothing more to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's go on, please, then, same topic and the same area, to the document you were shown, which is at 33 of the bundle, and it's P1502. This is the inspectors going back again on the 10th -- well, in fact they go back on the 7th and the 8th. And you have already looked at this document and you looked at in proofing. The second paragraph: "The following attended the first part of the work meeting at the CSB which was held on the 7th and 8th of August ... Stojan Zupljanin, Djuro Bulic" and yourself as assistant commander of the special police detachment. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not the assistant commander. You have a list and you can see my name there. I was present at the meeting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, why would the inspectors be told you were the -- well, you can't answer that one, I suppose. But it's right, isn't it, you were introduced as the assistant commander?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, anyone could have put anything on the record. By establishment, it's known what I was. I could not have held this particular office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to come and show you exactly why you were, in fact, the assistant commander. But you say anybody can write down anything. How on earth could somebody have written down your name as assistant commander of the special police without somebody having said that? It's not possible, is it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. It's a report someone wrote after the fact. It was written in Sarajevo on the 10th of August, 1992, and it was written by someone based on notes that they had taken. And perhaps because there was no commander, this is how they just formulated that I was the assistant commander. I had specific tasks, and I was not in this position. The fact that I was present is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Finally before the break, let me ask you this: The next -- the other gentleman there was a Mr. Samara. What was his role?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the police department. I really don't know. He was -- he had some kind of role with the uniformed police, but I'm not quite sure what it was. There is some kind of order there, but I don't know what it is. At this time I really can't recall what he was in the month of August. I don't know. I don't know what's written here. I just have to check, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says police inspector here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But I want to know why he was there. What was his function? Why was he at this particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How I would I know? It's a meeting attended by Djuro Bulic, the chief of the centre. There was Colonel Bogojevic on behalf of the army. It was a joint meeting with military security and with these inspectors. It had something to do with that decision to turn the unit over, complete men and its equipment, to turn it over back to the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You made a mistake there, didn't you, sir? It was to turn over the special police to the army. Because if they were part of the army, sir --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- they didn't need to hand back anything.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they had some joint equipment. We paid them. We had some men. We would not turn our men over to the army. Those who remain in the army would only be military personnel, and that was standard practice. We would bring back our men, those who were -- or used to be in that unit. That's quite normal procedure when something is being reorganised. It's normal for people to meet and see how things would wind up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Finally on this document, please, sir: "After introducing the decision made by the minister of the interior at a meeting held on the 6th of August, a large number of participants and, in particular, members of special police detachment command and platoon commanders, rejected all suggestions and insisted on preserving the status of the unit as was." Were you one of the people who rejected all suggestions?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in favour of rejecting all proposals, but if there was a particular position that was presented, it was probably conveyed to those men there what the positions of the members were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's not an answer to my question. But I take it you're saying that you didn't object.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's all I ask on that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Could we go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right, sir. I want to move to -- from Stojan Zupljanin's authority over the police, that issue, to the composition, in itself, of the special police. Can you look, please, first of all, at 65 ter 20337, which is 30A in your bundle. Now, this is - do you agree? - as you're familiar with the administration documents, a payment approval being issued for the special detachment? Do you agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't have the opportunity to see this before, but, yes, I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, well, there are a number of documents that Mr. Krgovic decided not to show you. Can you now move, please, to the fourth page in English and the fourth page in your language. This is the payment for June of 1992. And is it headed: The list of reserve police force members? Sir, do you agree the heading of this list is: "Reserve police forces members, detachment for special purposes"?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the list from June 1992, and this status was declared, but I think these people were never officially given those cards. I don't recall having quite -- because actually all, or 90 per cent of these are members of the military. I really couldn't say yay or nay, but I think that this is a list of the reserve police members. This is how they were christened, probably, in some documentation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, nobody, sir, as I put to you on Friday, was going to pay these men from police funds unless they were, in fact, reserve policemen. That's the reality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had to be some kind of legal basis. There had -- they to find something, and I think that this is the way it was done in the bookkeeping because these people over there had to record them as theirs, in order to be able to give them weapons and things. And so it's normal that they would be placed here, but, actually, it would be justification for expenditure of funds.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, before we move on from that document, can we just note some of the names on this June payroll. Do you see, at number 60 -- we need to go to the next page, please, in English and probably in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Zlatko Milankovic?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. At number 92, Radomir Sejmanovic?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radomir Sejmanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And some other familiar names that we'll come onto later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this please be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2412, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, please, have a look at the document will you find at number 29, 65 ter 20318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, before we leave this document, could we see the last page --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- because I'd like to see the number of persons listed here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. Go to the last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Or the page that shows the end of the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, yes. In English, it's at page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: 214, I see is the number of persons on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the eighth page. Yes, 214. And, in fact, the following documents, Your Honour, are just the -- we can see the payment, the balance of payments ... So let's go now, please, if we may, to 65 ter 20318. And can we go --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, do you recognise this as part of the administration for payment?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this document. I cannot recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, yes. Whether you've seen it or not, is this the standard payment document that would be drawn up by administration?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the forms were. If this is part of our administration, then that's it. It says here, "SSB Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's have, please --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then that must be that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's have a look, please, at the fourth page in English and on -- it's the third page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Tab -- sorry. It's tab 29.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, does that show that it's the list of the members of the police special detachment, security services Banja Luka. And are you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we perhaps go into private session just for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The document is up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, again, do you agree the special police members are being described as reserve police forces?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've seen that the other list contained more than 200 people and you saw how many people the special police had, so something is not quite right here. They were all recorded as reserve members, the actual active police and the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The reason that they are described as reserve or active police is because whatever they came from, whether it was the military police or the SOS, they became, did they not, reserve policemen? That was their war-time assignment?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a way to pay them their salary. This was done in such a way in the system, in order to justify the payment. There was a list of 270 people who were shown to be members of the reserve, in order to be able to receive their salary. And, here, the signature is not the signature of Stojan Zupljanin. Somebody else signed it for him. It states "for the chief." "For the head."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Leaving that aside. Do you agree, whether, as you say it was a strategem or not, all the people who were members of the special police received a war-time assignment as members of the reserve police, if they were not already professional police officers?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know whether they were placed on the war-time schedule or not. From what I can see here, this is some sort of formal justification for them to be able to receive their salary. I don't know if their registry cards were taken, changed, if anything was made --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because these things would have to be in their cards, that the cards were taken over on such and such a date, or that they were requested to be placed on the war-time schedule, or something like that. I never -- I don't know if these people were ever officially requested to be placed on the war-time schedule. I'm talking about the practical situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And legally, if they were assigned to the police or the reserve police, then they came under, did they not, the authority - obviously indirectly because they had people in charge - of Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the legal aspect, if they were placed on the war-time assignment list, then they did have some connection with Stojan Zupljanin. But I'm talking about the actual situation on the ground. That they were part of the command that was militarily oriented.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that document please be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, having regard to the number of light documents that we already have do we need to add this to the list?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it's got -- it is signed off by Stojan Zupljanin who is the accused in this case and who calls them reserve police. Whereas the other was just a list. On -- I'm sorry, I take that back. Somebody on his behalf signed. Whereas, the other one just said "reserve police" at the top. This is slightly different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2413.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the question of identity cards, where you spent a number of pages attempting to explain it and confusing everybody in the court, at 25462 of the transcript, which was on the Wednesday. Judge Delvoie asked you a number of questions about this. And what you said, at page 25462, in answer to Judge Delvoie: "If you look at these -- those identification cards they weren't really official IDs. They were just some kind of certificates with the same text that could be found on real official police IDs, and that was one of the problems." "Judge Delvoie: Are you telling me now that those people were not police officers?" Your answer: "They basically were police officers because they were issued IDs by the centre, but in essence they were a military unit." Well, either they're police officers with an official identity cards or they're military people. Which was it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already explained what the situation was. We had problems with people falsely introducing themselves. And this was regulated in a way by providing them with some sort of formal IDs which were created quickly and were not like in form or in content the actual IDs. But that then prevented even larger abuses than the ones committed when they didn't have any of these IDs. They were blue. They had two pages. And the back -- the photographs that they were issued were inside this booklet. This was something that all the actual policemen carried. But these other ID cards were made quickly, to give to these people so that they could enter the facility and to create among them a feeling of responsibility. As I said, during that time, it was some sort of transitional measure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, let's just have a look, shall we, of what these ID cards actually looked like and said. Can you have a look, please, now at document 2D00072. You will find it at tab 37. Now, this is, in fact, the criminal report that was rather hopelessly brought against these men that we discussed earlier, two of whom were broken out of prison, and we'll come back to that. We may as well note while we're at it that what you described as just an incident involving a car was actually a robbery, wasn't it? Have a look at the first page. Have a look at the first page, sir.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Under Boskan and the rest, they were being attempted -- an attempt was made to prosecute them for robbery, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criminal act of robbery.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now let's look, please --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I didn't catch the translation?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was for all three, this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, let's move but I'm going to come back to that because I want to deal with the criminal acts committed by the special police separately. I want you to look, please, at a photocopy of the identification card, which is in English --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately, the Defence have got this translated and give it page numbers. But it says 1D00-6081 in English at the bottom. And in B/C/S, it is 0 -- 6050, to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is the card, is it not, of Ljubomir Jokic?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can we have the next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the back of the identification card, which we can see in English there. The bearer of this identification card is authorised to request to see identification from citizens, bring them in before the relevant organs, stay there and perform a certain without a search without an order from the [indiscernible], carry fire-arms, use them under conditions provided by law, et cetera. Would you agree that gives them powers as police officers?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, they were issued with official ID cards. Somebody copied the text from the real documents and put them here. But this ID did not look like the proper official ones and it wasn't a proper official one. This text was simply copied from there. And because they were abusive, later it was decided to accept into the police only people who had been through training, who would be told that this does not literally standard, that they would be needed to be aware of very last remark, "use under the conditions provided by law," that all of this did not apply to them. All those who had gone through a six-month training course could then join the police, those who had the aptitude for it, and they were told that this did not literally apply, that there was certain rules of conduct that they had to respect. It was some sort of improvised measure that did not actually prove to be better. We did have problems with those policemen, members of that unit, who actually had to be criminally charged because they did not act pursuant to the law, and they were not really trained adequately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Quite -- can I say, I'm not disputing that at all, sir. I accept entirely that because you were in a time of conflict - I say "you, the policemen - they accepted people into the police who otherwise they would not have. But the fact is, sir, isn't it, that these men, however ill-trained, however criminal, were in fact police officers, described as police officers, issued with identity cards as police officers. That's the reality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was an identity card. They didn't get police IDs. Police IDs were blue with the real insignia of the state and everything, and this is more of a pass. Only it has this text on it, the same one as on the official ID, but this isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, I'm sorry, exactly. That's an identical -- it is word for word the text that was on -- when you say "official," let's put it this way, the IDs that had been issued before to the police, because, can I put it to you -- Well, first of all, is that right, that the text is identical?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so. The real official ID had something similar on it. And the one who made these documents probably copied it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Identical, sir, not similar. Identical.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. That's what I said. I don't have an original official ID here. That's why I can only suppose. But I mean, there's nothing much to discuss about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if they -- if they were not police, and all that was required for them to -- to get an identity card, a photograph, to allow them entry to the barracks, this text would be totally unnecessary, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle. But as I said, when -- whoever made these chose this layout.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, let's look at what we've established through the documents. They are described as reserve police. They have identification cards which, on the back, has -- has an identical wording to other police passes. I don't know whether you're aware of this, are you -- this expression, have you ever heard the expression, "If it walks like a duck, if it quacks like a duck, then it's probably a duck"?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't heard that one before. That's interesting. But this was about something else. Officially they were on the registry as such, but I told you about the formal aspect, and the real aspect, and what could be found in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I want you to go to the further payment record for July, please, which you'll find at tab 17; 65 ter 20317. I want you to have a look, please, at page 3, I think it is, and number 31. And it's page 2 in yours; page 3 in ours.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Nikola Damjanovic. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know ... I don't really know 90 per cent of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Number 47, Slobodan -- well, the name at number 47; did you know him?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. The surname is familiar. But if you would show me a photograph, I wouldn't be able to recognise the man. I did see those guys, but I didn't have dealings with them, really. I paid them their salaries, and, in most cases, somebody -- somebody of them would sign.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Can we go to the last page, I'm sorry. Do you see there in the last page, very last page in both, English and B/C/S? Last page. No. The last page should be page 12 in English - thank you - and ... Do you see there Novak Zeljkovic was paid based on approval by the chief of centre?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. True.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know. Somebody was added here for some reason. I made a note that he was paid based on approval, and that the money for him was taken over by Captain Dubocanin. That was my remark. Because I didn't give the money to him personally. I gave it to Captain Dubocanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, did you check personally with Stojan Zupljanin that it was okay to pay this guy?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither did Stojan Zupljanin. I paid out the money. And I have the certificate here, that Captain Dubocanin received that money, and I suppose that he knew the man.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry. It says based on approval by the chief of centre. Before you paid the money, did you speak to Stojan Zupljanin and say you approve it -- say, Do you approve it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how should I know now? It's been 20 years. I can only see that I made this remark here. He may have brought a piece of paper - I mean, Dubocanin - or simply told me so. I really don't know. It's been 20 years. It's hard for me to be sure why I made a certain remark.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be entered and marked, please, exhibited and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2414, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, we're going to have to go back for a moment to the identification card which is, please, 1D6 ... oh, no, sorry, I see it's a different one. Could we have up, sorry. Could we have -- it's not on my list but something's being pointed out to me for some reason. 1D6082. Your Honours, it is to do with the issue of identification cards. Sorry about this. I've just been, as you'll gather, sent a note about this. 1D006082, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just confirm, I'm not sure -- because I believe that is the same one we've just shown. I see it is part of 2D. But can we -- I'm still not at all clear why -- could I look at the back of this, in B/C/S. Just a moment. No. All right. Your Honours, I'm sorry. [Indiscernible] listening to people sending you e-mails into court. Can we move on, please. Could we now look, please, at where some of these officers came from. Could we have a look, please, at 65 ter -- sorry. Yes. And I'm sorry, Your Honours, it is my fault, and I'm now wasting some of my precious time. Can I go back, please, to the list that we were originally looking to, which has just been admitted as an exhibit. 2414.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 17 in your bundle. Do you see there number 10, Aleksandar Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He was an ex-member of the SOS, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. You knew that he was an ex-member of the SOS, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, I have never seen an official list of these people. I cannot be fully sure who was a member. There were rumours about a number of them being SOS men, but I cannot swear on it. I suppose that he may have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you knew that, didn't you, because he was one of the leaders of the SOS, wasn't he, when Banja Luka was barricaded in April?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there when -- at the time of these barricades, so I really don't know. It was an organisation I wasn't part of. I cannot give you any official information because I don't have it. If you have information that he was, all right. But I don't have such information. I was never at a meeting of any such association.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I mean, I'm not going to show it to you. But, in fact, he appears in the full report as one of the leaders that was done by "Glas" on the 4th of April. But I want you to look at somebody else that you identified at number 31, Nikola Damjanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, could we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It doesn't show the name, Your Honours, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yeah, I know that. You -- the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He participated as an SDS member in the arming of the Serbian people in Dvor Na Uni and Glina, and then he joined apparently the -- well, it says on behalf of the 1st Krajina Corps Military Police under the knowledge of Commander Milan Stevilovic, et cetera, et cetera. And then he apparently personally arrested the secretary of the SDS, who was spying. And then on the invitation of the War Presidency of Banja Luka as part of the military police, he participated in the attack on Derventa, returned to Banja Luka, where during the blockade of the town by the SOS forces he protected vital facilities as an SOS member. So would you agree that you signed off saying that this man, under -- there's no doubt about it, was a member of the SOS?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my signature, and his superiors stated this information about him as true. You can see that it says up there that Colonel Stevilovic coordinated all these activities, as I had said. Which means that it was all organised by the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You see, let me say again what the reality was. Accepting that it was a time of war, wasn't it, special police accepted anybody who volunteered to join, whatever their background. Didn't they? And you, as one of the leaders, I suggest, accepted anybody.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, what I see in front of me, this profile with regard to the combat activities, is given -- or issued upon the request of the said person. This was obviously stated by his fellow fighters because he had some -- had a difficulty with speaking. He seems to be a person with -- with a post-traumatic syndrome, as it is called today. Some places are mentioned here, but I have never visited them myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Look, sir, that's not the question I asked you. I asked you whether, in fact, in reality, the special police carried out the -- the -- the -- the leaders of the special police detachment carried out no checks on anybody and was prepared to accept anybody from any background? That's the reality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Either yes or no, please --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- person has been subject to checks. He was a member of some unit or other. And after his injury ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And, indeed, I'm suggesting to you that he was, as I've suggested all along, not a member of the military but a member of the police. If you look at the second paragraph, in the middle, after this, he put himself forward as an experienced fighter as a candidate for the special police unit where he was accepted on the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this also said that, on 4 July, he had a traffic accident, and after that, he suffered from -- he had psychological and physical difficulties --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I agree -- I agree --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what he stated. You must bear in mind that this was probably an aggressively behaving PTSD case so they would have issued him any certificate whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. The point is, sir, is that it's not that he was not a member of the military. He was put forward as a candidate for the special police and he was accepted. That's what this says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "experienced fighter." He volunteered as a candidate for the special police. But to who? To Stevilovic? Or to Markovic? Because they're volunteers. They accepted to go to the special police as soldiers, which means that Stevilovic selected them among the volunteers, and that's the meaning of this sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same as in the police. We also had volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, may this be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2415, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now I want to move, please, to deal with the question -- well, can I just ask -- I'm going to ask you to look over the break, the next break, at some photographs with names of members of the special police. But I want you to have a look at them before I ask you any questions because I'm going to move to resubordination. You say that all of the special police at all times were resubordinated to the military; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, -- well, let's get this straight then. What are you calling combat activities?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat activities, in principle, went on all the time. That's why I said that it was resubordinated. The entire unit was in areas where there were combat activities of the army. And in these areas, the unit was resubordinated, which is the standard designation for this type of activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
