utterances.text: All right. Are you saying that anywhere where the unit went, even if given no task at all by the military, it was still resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, in principle, it didn't go anywhere without the military present because it was war time. The military always had the main role in all these activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, no, I'm sorry. Is it your assertion that simply because the military was there in the area, even though your unit was given no specific task to carry out by the military, it was still resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle, wherever it was, or, rather, wherever there was war-time activity, in the entire area, the army had priority. They were more powerful than we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Look. Listen very carefully to the question. Is it your assertion that if you were carrying out any task, for example, interviewing prisoners, even if given no direction or order by the military, you were still resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, it depends what they do. Interviewing people means doing the job of state security or public security. If the interview is about a situation, then the chief of state security is informed but, simultaneously, military security is informed. There was this link between state security and military security.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, there's a difference, and you know yourself there's a difference. I'm not suggesting for one moment that the military and the special police, particularly in Kotor Varos, were not acting together. But I'm asking you about what you have been asserting, which is that, you, the special police, were resubordinated in the proper, legal, technical term, every time you carried out a task. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. The word "resubordination," was that a word suggested to you by Mr. Zupljanin, for example, in a phone call?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "resubordination" is a standard term applicable in military terminology, and I'm an army reserve officer; therefore, I use this word.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And just tell us, would you, please, in your own language, what is the word you use?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say resubordination or subordinational units. But the official technical term is resubordination, and also legal, and it is applied in military terminology, and I finished a military school, and we were given proper instruction about this. And it is also contained in the rules of the department for preparations. There were some guide-lines concerning that, the department preparing war plans and similar items.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to -- but I just want to put one more thing to you on your relationship with Mr. Zupljanin. It's right, isn't it, you and Mr. Zupljanin were very close?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that we never had coffee together. In our part of the world, when you say that you don't have coffee with someone, it means that you -- you are not close to those people, and I also might add that I never went to celebrate his family patron saint's day. And after that -- all I would like to add that I never went to his home. The only place I saw him was in his workplace --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and in passing. Therefore, we never socialised, and I cannot say that we were particularly close.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, can you think of any reason why Mr. Radulovic came to see you while Mr. Zupljanin was on the run to see if you knew where Mr. Zupljanin was?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Radulovic was an intelligence officer, and he probably tried to find a contact person. I was not that kind of person, and he found someone else. And I suppose that he conducted the same interview with hundreds of other people as the one that he had with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's look, please, at one example of -- of what, I suggest to you, is resubordination proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have look, please, at 65 ter 754.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Document number 41 for you, sir. Now, I'm not suggesting, sir, you would have ever seen this order, but you knew who the 1st Light Infantry Brigade were in Kotor Varos, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that its name was the 1st Light Infantry Brigade, but I was aware of the fact that there was a certain military formation there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Commanded by somebody called Dusan Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Never came across him in all your time in Kotor Varos? As the head of the military down there? Or the head of the 1st -- the 1st Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had any direct contacts, apart from with the people that I already named. I personally saw Colonel Peulic, then Stevilovic, but as for the others, let me add that at this entry check-point there was another officer. But as for the others, I didn't have any contacts or any dealings with them. And to put it simply, I don't remember this name. But as I said, I knew that there was a military unit in Kotor Varos. However, what was its strength and who their commanding officer was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at number three, paragraph 3 of this order. A platoon -- do you see the words: "A platoon of the Banja Luka CSB service centre" --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Page 3? Give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Third paragraph, please. Not page 3. Third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Just a moment, please. Paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: A platoon of the Banja Luka CSB will engage in action in coordination with the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade in the direction of Kotor. Now, a platoon of what from the CSB? This is the 30th of September.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 30th of September --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 24th. 24th of -- 24th, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. What it says here, the CSB platoon. Maybe that's what they called them after the change-over of the situation. After the 29th of September, there was no police unit or any platoons. When they say CSB platoon, they probably meant those who took over on the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It makes sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to suggest to you in a moment that the special police were not disbanded on the 10th of August at all. But I want to deal with this. Right. Now, there, sir, that is a classic example, isn't it, of a police squad, or whatever you like to call it, being used by the military to carry out combat?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the time when this was written, there was no such units. In other words, it can only refer to the unit that was handed over to them on the 10th of August, and that's how they called it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's fine by me. Leave aside the 10th of August, the -- those members of the special police that were handed over to the army were engaged in combat, and clearly not as members of the army, because otherwise there would have been no need to say that, would there?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, your construct is completely erroneous. You might call it what you wish, as some were called Burcani. But they were members of the army or Territorial Defence. However, they had their colloquial name. Similarly this one was from the CSB or taken over from the CSB. I don't know how else to explain to you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, sir, stop. Stop --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The three platoons numbering 100 men were left behind and they were in this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, stop, sir. If they had been handed over on the 10th of August and were members -- proper members of the army, they would no longer be described, would they, as the Banja Luka CSB unit? They had been absorbed into the units.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably they maintained the same strengths divided into platoons as it had been before. And for easier communication, orientation, that's what they were called.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But last question on this document: Do you accept that -- that what's being talked about here is actual fighting, combat?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order to launch an attack, to engage in combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. We'll leave that document, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, can I ask that that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2416, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be given the document which is at tab 62, number -- doesn't matter about the number. I would like him to have a look at it over the break, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before it's given to the witness, can the Prosecutor please tell us what this document essentially contains. Is it something that was prepared by the Prosecution and then they ask the witness to deal with it? What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was disclosed some time last year. It's a set of photographs that come from the CSB in Banja Luka, that were collected together, and where such identification was possible of the names, that was made from the records. It is from the CSB Banja Luka. Mr. Koehler made a lengthy statement about it sometime last year and that's when it was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I wanted to know was who entered those names and who compiled this document. That is what I wanted Ms. Korner to explain to us. The witness should be shown a proper document, not a compilation that contains certain remarks or inputs from somebody else. So if the witness asked to identify some other people based on this kind of compilation of the document that had been processed or -- or worked over six months ago, I don't think that this is enough for identification. Your Honours, this is the essence of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if I understand Mr. Krgovic correctly, it's that the witness should be given a clean copy of the set of photographs. Is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I don't agree, I am afraid. This witness is entitled -- had -- was -- worked with this group throughout its existence. He is able to say whether or not the names which were assigned by a member of the staff in Banja Luka, the -- [indiscernible] is correct. If not, which are not correct. I would also like him to see whether he can identify himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So the witness may have the folder of photographs and we see where we go at the break. So we go into closed session so that we can take the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, sir, over the break, you've had a chance to look at the photograph assembly of the members of the special police, which is - I've got the number so we can just get it up on the board - 20339; tab 62. Firstly, are you able to confirm that where they've been identified, those identifications are correct?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that they were accurately identified because I honestly don't know some of those people. I can only speak about this part that I am familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, first of all, do you appear anywhere?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen a photo of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Have a look, please, at the page that is marked at the top, 06785419.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the photographs there of Ljuban Ecim are of him?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put a circle around the names of the people whom I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to name any names, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, just -- sorry, sir, you can't do that. All right. Can I --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Usher, could you take it off him and I will just read out the ones -- if the witness would prefer, it can be done in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you prefer this be done in private session, sir?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would prefer to have it in private session, and we can expedite things.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have up again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because I've now worked out what I was being told to show you, to 2D0072, at document 37.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we need the page, which is 1D006052 in the file.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the identification card, isn't it, of Radomir Boskan?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroslav Dragojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, wrong one. It's signed, isn't it, by Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At least I suppose that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, no. You recognise his signature because you were able to say on another occasion that was not his signature. That's his signature, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we blow it up, enlarge it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, it's written here. Yes, I can identify the name Zupljanin. Yes. That's his signature. It was too small before, but now it's okay, and I can see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's all I wanted to ask you about that document. Again, I wanted to complete this business of resubordination as you have told us about. You discussed, didn't you, with -- well, first of all, can we have a look at a document, which is, I think, at P27 -- it's P275, at 45 -- at tab 45. No, sorry, it's P1096, I beg your pardon, at tab 45. Sorry. Yes. On the front, it says: "Order, Ljuban Ecim, aka Car."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When we look at the next page, could we not have it go out on the screen while we stay in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is dated the 31st of December, 1992, and it's signed, do you agree, by Stojan Zupljanin over the signature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm advised this is a public exhibit so if there is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking -- no, I'm just asking because I'm going to ask a question about it. I appreciate it's not supposed to be under seal, but I need a question about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So do we -- because it's a public exhibit, do we have to go into private session for you to ask your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is it not just good enough for the document not to be shown on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That depends on the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Is Your Honour -- rather than waste time, let's go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What number is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 12A. Don't worry. It's one tiny bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you highlight, please, at the bottom of the page, Bosanska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 24th of May, 1992. It is reported that Lukic, Mirko Lukic was seriously injured in a car accident. That's right, isn't it? You knew

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I think we should go to the private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, that is what the Court Officer was just alerting me to. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That -- this is at page 25421. When you were being asked about your duties, that you had administrative duties, and you said: "I also gathered certain information about members of the unit, and in some situations I conducted interviews regarding complaints against members of the unit." From whom were there complaints?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The complaints mostly came in the form of dispatches from the Banja Luka public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Apart from the dispatches from the Banja Luka security station, did you receive complaints from any other source or have complaints passed onto you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a situation once that somebody came specifically to report, a citizen came to report something at the Rakovacke Bare command and I informed the superior officers about this. I think that -- well, I said I saw Mr. Lukic only once, and I think that that was that time when he was at the command. Later I saw him around town but I never saw him at the command again, at Rakovacke Bare command. Perhaps he would come and go and go to the field somewhere else, but at that time he said that all the members should be lined up and that person who claimed that there was some crimes committed by some members, he was asked to see if he could recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we did the lineup. And the man looked at everybody and didn't recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's move on to rather more serious complaints, shall we? First of all -- no, I'm not going to ask that question because we have to go into private session. Can you have a look, please, at P567, which is at number 11 of the binder. Did you ever investigate the complaint that came from Bosanski Novi that, in May, when they'd been sent -- the special police had been sent to Bosanska Kostajnica, a large number of citizens complained about the work of the members of the special unit who entered houses by force, beat up the menfolk and so on. Did you carry out any investigations to a complaint from another police station?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this document for the first time, this is not a document that I saw before, so I never acted pursuant to it. I didn't carry out an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When it's addressed to Ecim personally, are you saying that he never passed this on to you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I never had this in my hands before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... report a beating, it's a report of the next paragraph Mr. Ometlic had a lot of money, a watch and glasses taken. If we go to the next page, please, in English and also, I think, in B/C/S. Then there was stealing a car, which seems to have been habitual for your police. Beating up Mr. Aljovic, et cetera. And then at the end we see there were two Official Notes by Stojan Bjelajac. Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes, I see it, at the end, at the bottom. Bjelajac, Stojan, special police member.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he was a member of the special police, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states here: Report on the stay of the special unit from the commander of the special staff, Novkovic Mirko, and two Official Notes by Stojan Bjelajac. I don't know if they're his Official Notes or not. It's a little bit odd, this. I don't know what to say, really. I never received the document --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do anything in relation to it. And there is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you whether the gentleman mentioned there, Mr. Stojan, with the unpronounceable surname, was a member of the special police, to your knowledge, as described in this ...

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you see, he was one of the names that you were asked about when you looked that long document from Mr. Tutus. And --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I had the document with information about who was in the detachment and who wasn't. If they were in the detachment, you would be able to see that right away, according to the alphabetical order, and then I would issue information on the basis of that. Because I didn't know anybody just like that, off the top of my head. It would be very strange if I knew 150 people off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You were shown this complaint about him and you were specifically asked whether he was a member of the police and you said, No, he wasn't. I can tell because he was a member of the --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to ask Ms. Korner to pay attention to how she is addressing the witness. I would kindly ask her not to shout at the witness and to address him in a kind manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I agree. No, I apologise, Your Honours. I'm afraid I let my irritation at the constant drivel get the best of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked in -- by Mr. Krgovic about Stojan-what's-his-name and you said he was not a member of the special police, that he wasn't in 1993, but he was, wasn't he, in 1992, at the time when this complaint was released -- made?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that he wasn't on the list. I didn't have him on this list as a member. Perhaps he was there in the period before the list was drawn up. This list that I had, if the person wasn't on it, then the person was not a member of the special unit. Because it was a list that I received in 1993 from Djuro Bobic. And somebody had already made notes on it, and then I also did, on the basis of what I managed to find out. It's a simple list. When I was answering, I had both lists in front of me and I could easily see whether it was there or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, I assure you that Mr. -- your assertion, sir, was wrong, and you now see that it was totally wrong, wasn't it? He was, indeed, in 1992, a member of the special police.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please give me a document so that I could see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'll -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have a look -- no, I'm come back to that because I don't want to waste any more time. I'll come back to that after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Let's have a look at the next complaint, please. P659; document 13. This is somewhat ironically, I suppose one could say, a complaint from Simo Drljaca on the 13th of June where we hear the same theme. The unit whose members were commanded by the gentleman who is named there was not able to control any -- exert any control over the conduct of his troops. That was the main reason why the troops assigned duties at Omarska behaved with such extreme negligence. What they did there had least of all to do with security, arbitrary arrest, interrogation, abuse of prisoners, theft of their money, jewellery, et cetera, et cetera. The help we received from the special unit of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre during the attack on Prijedor was valuable, but after the joint action of the army, the special unit and our police, I received many complaints about the conduct of the special unit. Now this was addressed to Stojan Zupljanin. Did he pass that complaint on to you to investigate?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not conveyed to me personally. I'm trying to remember. I think that there was some kind of back and forth between the special and the local police. They were quarrelling, so it turned out to be a quarrel between them. I think both of them behaved improperly, but there were stories. I think somebody did conduct that procedure. I think this was on the 13th of June. I don't remember any disciplinary proceedings on this matter. I don't remember conducting anything like that. It was probably at the time when there was nobody there to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what do you mean it was a quarrel between the local police and the special police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, this was a feature, that, very frequently, like kids when they have a quarrel, they were accusing each other about things, something like, Give me my dolls back. I remember there were things like that happening in cafes, because the active-duty police considered themselves to be gentlemen and these other people were considered as military riffraff. So often they would do all sorts of things to each other. They would be reporting on each other. I don't know exactly what this was about. Perhaps if I had more information I would be able to see what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you -- this is -- it is absolutely clear -- you know what happened at Omarska, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it, but I didn't have the opportunity to see Omarska. I heard that there were incidents there, but I wasn't able to see it. I was out in the field. I confirmed where I was. I cannot give you my positions on places where I did not go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You know full well, don't you, that there was a -- let's call it a detention centre for the moment at Omarska which was run by the police. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I wasn't there. I cannot say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, stop.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be pointless for me to talk about Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Did you know at the time that the police had a facility at the Omarska mine? Not whether you went there. Did you know?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about it at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But a letter arrived saying that people who are being held at Omarska, prisoners, are being abused by your special police. Did you take any action yourself to investigate?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I didn't have this information, and, as I said, there were stories that they had a quarrel over there with Simo Drljaca. I really don't know what happened. I didn't have the opportunity to elaborate that further. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And this gentleman, Slobodan Strazivuk, do you know him to be a member of the special police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The surname is familiar. I think so, yes. I would have to look -- I mean, if he was on that list, then he definitely was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you know he is on the list we've looked at already once today. Number 47 on document --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you didn't do anything about that complaint either. Let's look at the next complaint. Perhaps one of the more serious ones you may think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, at P81.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Tab number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Crisis Staff, 26th of June, where Dr. Gajanin is informing the Crisis Staff of the -- of the situation as regards casualties and reported on what had been done on the premises of the health centre by members of the special unit, which he had tried to prevent but was driven away at gun point. Djekanovic said that last night he told Dubocanin about everything going on at the health centre and in town and had been assured by him it would be prevented. He said that all these questions had to be cleared up and information provided on the behaviour of the members of the special unit at the meeting with Zupljanin, the chief of the CSB, scheduled for tomorrow. Mikic said that the Crisis Staff had discussed the behaviour of the members of the special unit on several occasions and shown itself to be unable to influence them, and he asked Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic to help solve this problem. He also said this kind of behaviour could endanger the whole operation and make life more difficult afterwards. At the end of this item, the president said what had been done yesterday must not happen again. This kind of behaviour by members of the special unit and individuals on our side must be dealt with and they must be put under control. Now, you were asked about this incident by your own counsel. Are you telling the Court that being in Kotor Varos as you were in the month were June, no one told you about the killing of unarmed men outside the health centre?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am hearing about this for first time at the Tribunal. While in Kotor Varos I did not see a single person that was killed. I saw one wounded person that I took to the medical centre. I did not see anybody being killed. The only dead people that I saw, and this was not in Kotor Varos, were people who were killed and who were brought to Banja Luka for the -- for identification, and these were people from the special corps. I mean, this is something that I am prepared to answer questions with the use of a polygraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure you are able to, as you talked in graphic detail about that repellent video we saw. I'm not asking whether you saw the dead bodies but whether anybody told you Stojan Zupljanin, Dubocanin, Mr. Djekanovic, Mr. Pejic, Inspector Pejic, that members of the special police had cold-bloodedly murdered not less than 18 people outside the health centre?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying that I didn't have that information at all. Nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So Stojan Zupljanin --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stojan Zupljanin, who has been called for a meeting or they're having a meeting with him, never said, Go and investigate who was responsible for the killing so that we can bring charges against these men?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am seeing this for the first time. I mean, not the first time but this story, now, nobody ever told me that this happened. So how could somebody tell me to do something if they didn't even tell me that it happened. There's no logic to that. And I didn't know that anything like that had happened either, nor do I see here that anything like that had happened. You're saying that an incident is mentioned here in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me assure you that from other evidence that is what is being discussed, and you'd say you never heard, ever, until this Tribunal started about the killings outside the health centre?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And on that note, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, before we take the adjournment. Although the witness, to my mind, has indirectly answered the question, for my own satisfaction could I have an answer to the -- Mr. Witness, the question that counsel put was -- she said, "Stojan Zupljanin, having called for a meeting never said, Go and investigate who is responsible for the killing so that we can bring charges against these men?" I'm not forgetting your response but could we have a direct answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never heard of this incident, so nobody could tell me about it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody ever told me about it. I don't know. So I really couldn't, since I didn't know, nor did anybody tell me, that something like that had happened. So I couldn't have received any kind of order in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the break and come back for the extended session at 2.35. And we will sit until 4.05. We go into closed session to take the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, let's continue on the topic of complaints. Could you have a look now, please, at the document which is number 18 in your bundle, and it's P1089. This is a document dated the 1st of July, 1992, and it's addressed to the chief of the Security Services Centre, from Mr. Josic of the SJB. And there's a number of documents. The first is an Official Note - can we go to the next page, please - of an interview with a member, an anonymous member, it would appear, of the special police. I'll just run through the names that he mentions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to the third page in English. And also -- and the second page in B/C/S. So we're on the same page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mile Todorovic, who took pistols. Mr. Vranjes, took money from bodies of dead police officers. Mr. Kojic, smuggling weapons. Mr. Milankovic, broke into an apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, we need to go to the next page in B/C/S. Then we see again Mr. Slobodan Strazivuk. That the complaint had come from Prijedor. Arms smuggler, stealing fuel. Opening fire on a man in a cafe. Mr. Grujic. Mr. Gajic. Vukadinovic. And then the next page in English, please. Danko Kajkut.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he a brother or cousin of Nenad, sir?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have been a relative. It's the same surname.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he is confiscating foreign currency. Apparently stealing cars. The commander of the Doboj unit now drives a white Mercedes 300. Come back to the Doboj unit in a moment. Stealing foreign currency, Mr. Divic, Mr. Sladojevic. And Mr. Boskan again, together with Mr. Krizanac and Mr. Marincic. Seizing passenger vehicles. Over the page in English again, please, and over the page in B/C/S. This time Mr. Nenad Kajkut has gone through several stolen vehicles so on and so forth. And then a gentleman who is making, I accept entirely, an anonymous complaint from the special unit says, Now they continue to do the same, but they've been joined in Kotor Varos by Ecim, the head of the special forces. They steal large quantities of leather, leather jackets, bags and the like. And then Dusan Dragojevic. Now, did you investigate any of these allegations?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was written by a platoon member who was expelled for being undisciplined. I know that there were stories about this. He wanted to spite the others, and he wrote down all sorts of allegations but we were unable to come by any proof. We didn't do anything special about this. The more so, since it was anonymous.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's take first things first. How do you know that this report was written by a platoon member who had been expelled?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People talked about it. They analysed it among themselves. I cannot remember the details now, but somebody was thrown out for lack of discipline and then drew up something like this. And we had no information to corroborate it. And everybody denied the allegations, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, sir, was the answer to my original question, did you investigate any of these allegations: Yes, you did?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was an investigation, but it didn't go in-depth. And the investigation showed that the person was unreliable and that he alleged all this just to harm everybody else and that it was unfounded. I didn't have specific reports about these cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But didn't you think, particularly, as, for example, Mr. Strazivuk, this is the second complaint there's been about him, didn't you think that perhaps you ought to carry out a thorough investigation as to whether this man should remain in the special police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever there was specific information, we would remove the persons involved from the war-time assignment. Whenever there was anything reliable. It says here that he took a large quantity of fuel, is involved in weapons smuggling. But -- or is in possession of a passenger car from Kljuc or Donji Vakuf. We had nothing we could use. There was a member from Western Slavonia who was removed for some reason. I don't quite remember what exactly it was, whether he made a mistake in his work or engaged in some activity of this sort. Because it was 20 years ago, after all. But there was -- there was something of this type, and then it was declared to be insinuation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Wasn't an allegation of arms smuggling a serious one? Because you've told us that people were selling arms to non-Serbs. Wasn't that something you thought deserved investigation?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to prove that, we would have had to find the one who bought the weapons and the one who sold them and everything else. So this is merely hearsay. There is no tangible evidence because there are no -- there is no information even about the type of weapons. And everybody we asked said they had nothing to do with these allegations, and this was that all this was merely malice.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, let's carry on and look at the next complaint, which is rather more official.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you go to the next page, please, in English, in the same document. And in B/C/S, it's the fifth page. And in English it's the eighth page. Yep.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 20th of June, three members of the Banja Luka special police unit, Mr. Racic and Mr. -- well, two members it looks like. And Mr. Makivic, both of whom were members of the special unit, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one, Makivic -- well, he must have been if it is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can assure you that in a document that are both listed as members of the 1st Platoon. It's one of the documents that has been produced as an exhibit. I can't remember. It's 54. But I don't want to go onto that. And then Baja Makivic telephoned, according to this official report, the CSB chief, Stojan Zupljanin, demanding that all five officers who had arrested Mr. Rakic at the SDK -- I'm not quite sure what he wanted but --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see what this is about because it's illegible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well. Do you see -- it's not -- I agree it is not a very good copy. Mr. Rakic, apparently had been threatening a police officer with -- threatened him with a pistol. Then Mr. Makivic actually telephoned Stojan Zupljanin apparently. Did you -- well, I mean the real question is - I mean, I don't think the details are that important, actually - were you given this to investigate, and did you do anything about it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot read what this says.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember an incident where two members of the special police, on the 20th of June, went and created a pretty un -- unpleasant scene at the SJB, and one of them personally telephoned Zupljanin about it? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, but I -- now I remember that a certain Racic fired a shot in his own mouth, and he has been disabled since. He probably wasn't in a normal state of mind. This may be this incident. I'm not sure that this is the same person, but I think that one Racic fired a shot in his own mouth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, not on this occasion. He pointed a pistol at the police officer. Anyway, you did no investigations into this incident that you can recall.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If an investigation was made, then there must be an Official Note about the person involved being taken off the war-time assignment, and whoever has been taken off the war-time assignment cannot be on the payroll for August.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, the fact is that he was on the document that we looked at before, and let's have a quick look at it again, regrettably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it's been given an exhibit number. It's at 54, tab 54. It was 20323. It is now Exhibit 2410. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 1st Platoon, and this, as we've already discussed, this document was prepared sometime after the 31st of July. At number 5, Gojko Racic. And I've lost the other gentleman now.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There is Gojko Racic at number 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I have lost, unfortunately, Mr. Makivic, although I thought I had him after ...

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see him here. But he must be somewhere, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Well, we all agree he is a member of the specials. Right. Can we move, then, to the next document, please, although there is a further complaint about another. Can we look now, please, at P85. That's number 19 in the bundle. I've just seen him. He is number 15, Mr. Makivic. This is back to the Crisis Staff, this time on the 2nd of July. Item number 3: "Considering the situation in the SJB public security and the behaviour of special unit members, Ljuban Ecim and Stojan Zupljanin are to be called for interview." Now, did Mr. Ecim or Mr. Zupljanin say to you after the 2nd of July, The special police in Kotor Varos are still, putting at its lowest, misbehaving. We need to investigate. And looking at above, it seems to be in connection with stealing cars and taking them to Banja Luka. Did they ever tell that you need to investigate the theft of motor cars?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this Official Note. I haven't seen these minutes, so I don't know. But I've never been tasked with this. Maybe somebody else did it, but I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. On we go. Right. This is the incident which we looked at briefly in relation to Mr. Boskan and his friends. Sorry, item 24, which is -- sorry. P584. Now, this incident you do remember, I take it, sir?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the incident that has to do with their being brought in.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The robbery, and then the arrest, and then the violent freeing of them. You recall that incident, I take it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, what actions, if any, did you take to investigate or get rid of these men? Or to prosecute.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was about these people that I went to the Banja Luka CSB and spoke to the centre chief. Actually, no. First to the centre chief, and then I spoke to Vladimir Tutus, the chief of the SJB, because the first information I got was that there had been an unfair arrest of the members. I received information from Mr. Tutus and I said, Well, if that is the case, then they should stay in detention. After that, there were those unpleasant activities and their illegal freeing, the illegal liberation. But later on, I think that there was -- that there were proceedings before a regular court. It must be somewhere in the documents that, after this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, yes --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the procedure was initiated and the judiciary bodies dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, in fact, we've already looked at, the document for the identification cards. But although a criminal report was launched, they were never prosecuted, were they, ever?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know how the whole thing ended, from the judiciary aspect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the document you were looking at with Mr. Krgovic, which is at your tab 48, and it's 2D63. It's the one with your writing on it, in part. Oh, no, sorry. It's the one with your writing on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is the typed-up version of it. I'm sorry, we need to go back -- I think it's P10 ... sorry. That's the typed-up version of the document we were looking at. It's P -- all right. I think -- I think it's easier because I know where this one is. So can you go, please, to -- can we have up on the screen, have the document at 48.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is the simply the typed version of the one that you were talking about earlier.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me a moment. 48?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is the typed --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. And it shows what happened to the special police detachment members thereof. If we go to number 13, Mr. Boskan, who was the first of these people, was wounded in a bar -- Slavonia Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This here -- yes, this means that they left our area and went to the TO of Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly -- what this document does is show what happened to members of the special unit after the unit was wound up. Number 24, please, which is the gentleman who you asked me to identify where he was on the list, he went off to Tajfun. Now 42, please, which is the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a company. This is a military post number. Stojan Bilajac went to military post number 7002 -- or 7007.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You know what Tajfun was, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 42, Mr. Dragojevic, who was the second accused person on that criminal charge, he went off to a military post, is that right? So it doesn't appear anything happened to him.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- this clearly shows that they were kicked out from the platoon. And the military accepted people although they had been kicked out elsewhere and there were proceedings pending against them, but that was no obstacle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First of all, it doesn't show they were kicked out at all because this is what happened to everybody after the special police were wound up, wasn't it, including -- your name appears on this list, as does Mr. Ecim's. It's got nothing to do with being kicked out. It is simply somebody noting down where these people went once the platoon was wound up. That's it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he wasn't kicked out, then there must have been a new official ID because his old one had been taken off him. I stand by my statement that he was kicked out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And number 79 is Mr. Jokic, who is the last person on that. And it's at page 4 in English. He goes off to a military post, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is that it's the 1st Armoured Battalion. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, clearly, none of those three people who had been arrested and been broken out, at this stage anyhow, when this list was prepared in 1993, had been prosecuted for anything, had they?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proceedings were initiated in 1992. You may not know, but our judiciary is very slow and overburdened with cases, so that years elapse until anything is done, before people are summoned to appear, and, of course, you can't hold somebody in detention for ten years for a crime about which there is specific information. The regular procedure was conducted by the SJB under the law and in accordance with its powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, lastly, Mr. Dusan Dragojevic, number 45, who was the fourth person with Mr. Boskan, Jokic, and Dragoljevic [phoen]. He actually went off to the MUP special police, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that he is registered with the special police detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Hmm. He went off to -- sorry. He went to the new one, didn't he? The one that was created under -- ended up under Karisik.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I don't know. I cannot confirm that. I first have to look at what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, never mind. Right. Now, please, let's have a look at the document that will you find at number 36, and which is P1295.25. Now I accept entirely, sir, that you won't have seen this. It's a 1st Krajina Corps report dated the 18th of August. Can you have a look under number 3: Situation on the ground. "In addition to pronounced activity by extreme Muslim and Croatian groups, our soldiers returning from the battle-field are increasingly often retaliating and exacting revenge on Muslim and Croat families suspected of having some of their members amongst the Ustashas or Green Berets. "Foremost in taking revenge are former members of the CZB and special detachments." Now I'm not sure, nor was the translator, what -- do you know what the CZB is?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Members of the CZB?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You don't know what it is either.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this stands for. Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did you hear any reports, given this is Celinac which was right bang next door to Banja Luka, of former members of the special detachments taking revenge?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I'm just reminded that it is -- shows that Jokic and Dragojevic received pay for -- there's a document which we looked at before. If they were suspended or sent out of way, having committed these offences, sent to the military, would they have been paid by the police?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the agreement was to pay off everyone as at the 31st of January, so distinction was made. However, as of mid of that month, they were beyond our competence, but it was agreed nevertheless, that everybody should be paid up to the 31st of January. So everyone who appears on this list received their pay. Because the proceedings that they were the subject of were still in progress. And I'm talking about prosecution and criminal proceedings. According to the labour law, they are entitled to a monthly salary regardless of the fact that proceedings were conducted against them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's been translated as you saying the 31st of January. You don't mean that, though, do you, you mean August?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. 31st of August. I probably misspoke or maybe it was mistranslated. But, yeah, it is possible that I said that. Anyway, it's the 31st of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you have a look now, please, two more documents to show on this. In fact, maybe even one. The document you'll find at number 3, which is P97. Again, this is the Kotor Varos Crisis Staff. 21st of August, 1992. Item 2: "President Djekanovic pointed out matters and problems to be solved, to the effect that the pressure and the provocation by certain members of the special forces ... directed against Muslim and Croat families in order to compel them to leave should be stopped." The special police went on, didn't they, throughout August, until they were properly disbanded at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're obviously trying to infer something that has no base.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. To whom was Mr. Djekanovic referring when he stated that "the pressure and the provocation by certain members of the special forces ..." The only people who had the name "specials" was the police, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: Provocations by individuals from among the ranks of special units. Perhaps there were such individuals among their ranks. However, from the moment they were handed over, we, as the State Security Department and the Public Security Department, had no jurisdiction whatsoever over such individuals. The entire of this unit, along with all the men and the equipment, was handed over to the Army of Republika Srpska, I think General Talic, as a result of which I personally have no specific information about and we didn't receive any. I had never seen a report of this kind, and I didn't know anything about this. Most probably this is about some kind of random group that was operating there, although they are not being specific about who they're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We better go into private session for the next suggestion I'm going to put to you, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told the Court that you had discussions with Predrag Radulovic about reports he was putting in. You were aware, were you, that he ran a group that was known as Milos?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you aware that he put in a report on the 9th of June. Have it up very quickly, please, P76. It's -- probably won't find it in your bundle unless it's been added. It's 12C.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, well, you'll have to a have a look at it - it's very short - on the screen.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where Radulovic says it was the SDS who's going to start an operation with the aim of taking over power and settling ethnic tensions. Whilst this operation is going on, individuals who are in possession of unlicensed arms should be handing those arms in. The operation should be carried out in a synchronised manner, with the help of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre. Are you telling the Court that you didn't know that it was the SDS in Kotor Varos planning to take over and that it was the CSB that was going to be there largely to help out?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this report probably comes from the connections that the Milos Group had with Colonel Stevanovic [as interpreted]. Probably at the time when he spoke with them, he gave them this information, but I was not aware of this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, why should this report come from -- do you mean Colonel Stevilovic?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Radulovic did some odd jobs for the military intelligence service of Yugoslavia, he even had some contacts with Belgrade, it is possible that he had received this information from a higher level, i.e., from Colonel Stevilovic. But, according to all the activities that were going on at the time, Colonel Stevilovic should have been informed about all the activities and should have been privy to all the plans pertaining not only to this area but to the area of the entire former Yugoslavia, and this had to do with these particular problems. Now, as for this factual takeover, it doesn't say here that this was to be organised by the SDS. He is here positioning himself as somebody who is making suggestions based on the suggestions received from us and from other sources. So it says soon an action of takeover of power by the SDS will take over which means in the aftermath of the elections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we can all -- we can all -- no, please, sir. This is June 1992. This is the day before, or two days before the takeover, sorry. It's got nothing to do with the multi-party elections, this, has it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has. It does have. Because it was said at the time that power and authority should be established in line with the results of the elections. And, as far as I know, the SDS was victorious in Kotor Varos. However, the authorities were not established. Because there were some obstructions in that respect. Maybe the former coalition partners failed to reach agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's not go into that. Were you aware that either the day before or on the same day that this note was produced by Radulovic, there was a meeting at the Banja Luka CSB to discuss what was going to happen in the takeover? Not at the military, sir, the Banja Luka CSB.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it could have been the CSB, the one who would organise that without the military. That would be impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because I'm suggesting to you, sir, I'm suggesting to you that that's what the evidence is until you came along, that it is clear that the major role in this operation was played by the Banja Luka special police together with the army, but they had a lesser role, I suggest, than the special police, and that, as I've said to you more than once, what you're telling this Court about Colonel Stevilovic and the organisation is not the case. So that is why I suggest there was this meeting in the Banja Luka CSB which was attended by Mr. Djekanovic, Mr. Komljenovic, Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic, Mr. Zupljanin, and others. Were you there?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember such a meeting. Anyway, I don't think I would have attended it. But there is something that you refuse to accept. Two platoons make up 60 men and it cannot be a bigger power than the army that Mr. Peulic and other structures such as the Territorial Defence, the civilian protection, and the reserve police forces of Kotor Varos had at the time. Their numbers were ten-fold the one of the 60.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The takeover on the 9th, when you went there, was -- succeeded without a shot being fired, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The takeover of power did not occur on the 9th but I think on the 11th. And there were no combat operations. We entered the town without any fighting and any shooting. I went to the offices of the CSB --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Don't --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- without a single shot being --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, stop. Stop. I think there's a mistranslation. I think you meant the SJB. I don't want -- all I want to establish is: You agree there was no resistance. That's it.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no resistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And thereafter, a process of arrests went on, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And after the non-Serbs had been arrested, those who had not fled into the woods, they were taken to various places, and they were beaten up, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, not all of them left. I already said that a large number of Muslims and Croats left. But if there hadn't been any Muslims or Croats, I wouldn't be able to talk to those 50 Muslims in Kotor Varos, which means that there were people who remained behind. Obviously, since I spoke with them. And I'm talking about Kotor Varos alone. I couldn't talk to the walls. I talked to live people and they remained behind, seeking protection from the extremists from their own ethnic community.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly to say that you organised the return of weapons to non-Serbs to defend themselves against their -- their own extremists? Is that what you're telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. And I assert that weapons were distributed to the citizens of Kotor precisely for that reason because they were being threatened by their fellow Muslims and -- members of their community --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Although, as we saw, one of the purposes of this operation, from the note that Mr. Radulovic wrote, was to collect weapons, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The plan was to collect the illegal weapons. If you have about 400 automatic rifles in such a small town, obviously indicates that something was wrong, particularly because all these weapons had been taken away without the approval of people who were in charge of them, that is to say, that the Territorial Defence and the reserve police took the weapons without the approval of the respective commanders. In other words, it was stolen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't mention the weapons that was bought.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. By this period, the 11th of June, the Territorial Defence had been transformed into a light brigade, hadn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I was not in such structures where I would know something like that, whether it was resolved at that time or at a later time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And indeed, one of the commanders of the light brigade was Stojan Zupljanin's cousin, I think it is, Captain Slobodan Zupljanin, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was a relative. I think they were related.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now can we go back, please, to beatings. You know, don't you, that people were being beaten up?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I said. When they were brought in, they were physically abused.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. They were being beaten up in the police station, first of all, weren't they? To your certain knowledge because I suggest to you, sir, you visited people in the cells. Or the rooms in which they were being held.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems that you're not quite aware of it. In this translation it says "prisoners." They were not prisoners. They were detainees. Second, I said that people had abused their authority during this incident and that this happened a number of times in the hallway, not in the rooms, in the hallway. When you go in, there was physical abuse of men. This is something that I have said. It's not in accordance with the law. It happened. These groups were not under anyone's control. There were a lot of members from the local area. I didn't know who was who, but the locals knew, so they were local men.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you, sir, first of all, that the beatings were taking place by police officers, special police and members of the SJB, not unknown groups of people who suddenly appeared in the police station. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What action did you take to stop the people being beaten up in front of you in the police station by whoever it was?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times I intervened because of the noise that could be heard in the hallway and because of these things that were happening. However, I had no authority over these men. Certainly, in my presence, in the room where I was conducting interviews, no one was hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You see, I'm not suggesting you personally hit anybody, sir. But what I am suggesting is that as you went into these rooms, people were complaining to you, first of all, that they were being beaten up.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. I asked people, everyone with whom I conducted an interview, I wrote down their particulars, their name, their particulars, and asked them whether they were beaten or not. And I wrote this if force had been implemented against someone, I did this as a professional policeman, and this is a normal procedure to be conducted like this. Some of them did not want to say that they were beaten but it was obvious that they had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. There was being held at one stage, wasn't there, in the police station, when you were there, a woman?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not interview any woman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'm suggesting, sir, not that you interviewed her but that she was being held in the police station, with men in the same room.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it. Maybe it wasn't that first day when I was there in that role.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, you were the -- forget about --

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there. I really didn't see a woman. I didn't talk to any woman. I conducted interviews with men who had weapons. I didn't see any woman with weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we start, please, with -- sorry, I'll just get the right number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: P1579. And can we start it, please, at 5 minutes, 40 seconds. Your Honours, it's on the -- there's a transcript available at tab 57.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Can we pause there for the moment. And perhaps we ought to go back. Go back just to the beginning of that. To the beginning -- at 5 minutes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just let us know when you spot Mr. Ecim, would you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that as Kotor Varos police station?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have the sound. Is it possible to have the sound a little louder?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And obviously, if you see yourself as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we just pause it for a moment?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: This is Ljuban Ecim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now you told us that you were all dressed in police uniforms and that Red Berets were completely different and part of Dubocanin or Stevilovic's thing. Isn't Mr. Ecim wearing a red beret?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see clearly. It's possible. There's some refraction there. Maybe if we can look at it some more and then I will be able to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a red beret.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Still Mr. Ecim?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is not a member of the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: SZ-002 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What's his name, then, please, sir? All right. Do you want to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause the video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ordinarily, had we started at the usual time tomorrow, the second session would begin at 10.45, so do I safely assume, Ms. Korner, that you having not completed by the time of today's adjournment, that that extra 15 minutes between 10.30 and 10.45 you would wind up and Mr. Krgovic could begin his cross -- re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That was said rather quickly. I've now lost it and so has the -- Your Honour said would I complete within 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I will. Definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
